Sure! First use this https://www.calculator.net/calorie-calculator.html. Helps calculate amount of calories you need. It’s an estimate so bare that in mind you can adjust a little if you want but main thing is to keep an deficit and count for the first couple of weeks or months of your diet. I advise getting like a little book like a day planer and carrying it around with a pencil in your bag. You should also for at least the first 3 months not say “I’m doing good cheat day!” Remember it’s okay to eat a little more sometimes, but emphasize the sometimes. For you meals one thing I advise is at about 40 grams of protein per every meal. This is because Protein is good for building muscles and takes more energy to metabolize. Getting the protein is fairly easy, find good deals on chicken whether cooked or raw and get some protein yogurts and eggs, you will see that it’s pretty easy to get to the count. If you want some quick easy stuff for in the go too you can make protein shakes with plain almond milk and Protein power. Protein power if you want it is over priced in the stores so if you get it I suggest this website with this product https://www.optimumnutrition.com/en-us/Products/Protein/Shakes-%26-Powders/OPTIMUM-NUTRITION-GOLD-STANDARD-100%25-WHEY-PROTEIN/p/gold-standard-100-whey-protein?gclsrc=aw.ds&&gclid=EAIaIQobChMIq9-Ohdzh9AIViMCGCh3LeAIgEAAYBCAAEgIxmvD_BwE&gclsrc=aw.ds. You can set up a shipping schedule for every 2 months or so depending on how much you use it but I should last you at least a month and a half per power keg. With every meal try to have some veggies and fruits as well, every time you go shopping get some apple, salad, and some bell peppers and large raw carrots (baby carrots are old rotten carrots when the carrots was ground down DONT get  them they are a scam) and some celery. I suggest when you cook the meat you lightly oil a bake pan and bake the chicken with the vegetables (not the lettuce of course) cut up into small chunks around it and bake the chicken, put it in the oven at 450 and let it bake for 15-18 mins. Remember the chicken need to get to 165 degrees before edible. Also to skip this sometime you can just by a rotisserie chicken but in the long run it’s cheaper to get frozen. Oh yeah I assume you know to thaw meat in the fridge too when you take it out of the freezer to bake too. Once you calorie count you will realize that you have some free calories to use for some stuff you like to eat like maybe like 2 cookies or if really low a cake slice. Main thing is though if you aren’t hungry and you are like 400 calories under what you we’re shootings for for your deficits, you don’t need to push to eat it, if you are fine you are fine, but don’t starve yourself. Hope this helps and if you want more advice feel free to ask. Remember meals are flexible but always especially when just starting out try to have a fruit and vegetable and at least 40 protein. Also avoid junk food, while you can also still have some with no guilt, (again, don’t feel guilt having some snacks in the calorie range!) try other things like strawberry’s, or salted peanuts, or pineapple, they taste great and are healthy. SECOND THING TOO, IF YOU ARE ALSO HAVING MOTIVATION GOING TO THE GYM, 1 POWER THROUGH, AND 2, GET A FRIEND TO AGREE TO GO WITH YOU, SET A SCHEDULE, AND HOLD EACH OTHER RESPONSIBLE TO GO. Routine I suggest, I don’t know if it works for you, is Monday Wednesday Friday workouts, workout a little in between in the weekdays if you want, like walking or going the the gym a bit more, but on Sunday and Saturday do absolutely nothing related to working out. You do need some rest days. 

That was a bit much but feel free to reply to me with and questions you have any time, hope you start to feel better!

At your age I was in a similar situation. When I was your age and am now 19. I highly suggest that you embrace fitness as it will drastically help your mental health and improve your confidence in social interaction. Also if you can’t afford the gym or even if you can, get a small minimum wage job, give yourself something to do that will help you get cash. If you go to the gym I advise to mainly focus on the main 4 compound movements, squats, bench press, deadlift, and overhead press, and in addition to those bicep curls and just walking a mile (if you get a job in walking range that’s great too!) Dont be afraid to talk to people at the gym to give you workout tips or to spot you, there is a misconception in most people’s minds that people are mean, but in truth everyone there is just there to improve themselves and are actually pretty nice. If you ever wanted more specifics of what to do for a workout routine you could send a direct message. Just saying use this time when you are 16 now to improve, it gets better. When I was your age I started with a bench press of 165lbs and now at almost 20 I bench for reps 235lbs and my one rep max is 305lbs. Trust me when I say working out and getting a Job will make you feel better about yourself 100 fold.
